title: Emacs Writing Machine
content_html:
chainsawriot

Home | About | Archive

Posted on Jul 25, 2026 by Chung-hong Chan

I like writing. Really.

However, I have problem finishing my drafts. As you might be able to read in my OKRs, I mentioned multiple times that I have quite a lot of blog drafts that I haven’t completed. I don’t want to blame anyone and it’s completely my fault: I have problem focusing on a task. I have an attention problem. In the past, I could blame things like Twitter for distracting me from getting shit done. But now, I don’t use any of these social media services anymore. I am running out of excuses.

I wanted to change my writing routine and would like to see if it would make a difference. Then, I watched a video by Veronica (of Veronica Explains) on her (new) writing setup. She reused an old laptop and made it a dedicated writing machine, or “writerdeck.” In that writing machine, she only used command-line only Debian and neovim (her preferred text editor). Her blog post has details on her machine. I find the idea very interesting and wanted to give it a try.

First, I needed a spare laptop. 1 In fact, over the years my wife and I have accumulated a few unused but still functional laptops. I decided to take my wife’s previous ThinkPad T440 with Intel i5 and 8G of RAM. 2 It is a perfectly capable machine, only it is unbelievably slow for my wife’s relatively simple tasks such as watching YouTube. Modern web browsers are memory hog. And this is exactly the category of software a dedicated writing machine doesn’t need.

I followed Veronica’s blog post and installed Debian without any desktop environment and kmscon. My first diversion from Veronica is that I use emacs. I just quickly pulled my emacs configuration on my main machine from Git and removed all configurations about programming. emacs launches extremely fast 3 and should be so. You know, people bought 386 back in the late 80s to 90s to do similar things: launching DOS and write with Word Perfect or Word Star. 4 There is no way that an i5 machine cannot do that perfectly as it is perhaps 1000 times better than a 386.

With my own configuration, it also has all the emacs packages that I need for writing. And in fact, not that many: I only need deft to organize my files and Markdown mode (sorry I don’t use org mode). I feel quite at home writing there. I don’t want to waste a lot of time customizing. So I don’t even want to install vterm and simply use eshell, as I probably don’t need to do a lot of command line works. The machine now directly boots to emacs (just put emacs in .bashrc). More concretely, directly to deft (just add (deft) to my emacs configuration file).

Another diversion from Veronica is how I get the text files from the writing machine to other machines. I do not want to set up syncthing to sync text files across machines. I don’t even want to have ssh server on any of my computers. My overkill solution is to just have a Git repository and have a remote on Codeberg. magit is also useful here to further reduce the command line usage. It is only my lack of imagination for using Git. Maybe in the future I will have something like rsync.

Then, I write. It is really great! It’s extremely snappy and extremely minimal. And I can really focus on the writing, rather than being distracted (and frustrated) by the bullshit on MS Teams about my work. I also don’t need to sit around my “work desk.” I can also write from my couch while watching Tour de France.

There are still some minor nitpicks that I want to fix for this setup. One is the blinking cursor of kmscon 10.0.1. I can be easily frustrated by any blinking cursor. I think it will be fixed in the next official release. I see it over the official GitHub repository. 5 Another nitpick is the emacs theme. Many emacs themes were developed for the graphical mode. I want to use a bright theme (e.g., solarized). But it displays quite badly on kmscon. But the default dark theme is fine.

With this new setup, I think I will be able to finish my backlog of drafts and also some new academic writing tasks.

  1. I did consider an alternative of building myself an oversized handheld computer with something like a Raspberry Pi Zero. But upon self-reflection, I don’t want to create more E Waste, as I have enough E Waste at home. I should reuse something that is otherwise E Waste, so that it is no longer a waste. ↩

  2. I bought it already preowned. ↩

  3. emacs is reasonbly fast that I don’t even bother to set up emacs server. And I should not need to launch emacs very often. ↩

  4. Some prominent writers still write in this kind of setup. The most famous is of course George R. R. Martin and his DOS computer with WordStar. ↩

  5. It is too much for me to compile kmscon on the writing machine. So, I will just wait. ↩

content_html_zh:
链锯战士

首页 |关于 |档案

发表于 七月 25, 2026 由 Chung-hong Chan

我喜欢写作。 真的。

但是，我在完成草稿时遇到了问题。 正如您可能会在我的 OKR 中读到的那样，我多次提到我有很多博客草稿尚未完成。 我不想责怪任何人，这完全是我的错：我在专注于任务时遇到了问题。 我的注意力有问题。 过去，我可能会责怪 Twitter 之类的东西分散了我的注意力，让我无法完成任务。 但现在，我不再使用任何这些社交媒体服务。 我已经没有借口了。

我想改变我的写作习惯，想看看它是否会有所不同。 然后，我观看了维罗妮卡（维罗妮卡解释）关于她（新）写作设置的视频。 她重新利用了一台旧笔记本电脑，并将其变成了专用的书写机，或“writerdeck”。 在那台写作机中，她只使用命令行 Debian 和 neovim（她首选的文本编辑器）。 她的博客文章详细介绍了她的机器。 我觉得这个想法很有趣，想尝试一下。

首先，我需要一台备用笔记本电脑。 1 事实上，多年来我和妻子积累了几台未使用但仍然可用的笔记本电脑。 我决定使用我妻子之前的 ThinkPad T440，配备 Intel i5 和 8G RAM。 2 这是一台性能完美的机器，只是对于我妻子执行相对简单的任务（例如观看 YouTube）来说，它的速度慢得令人难以置信。 现代网络浏览器非常消耗内存。 而这正是专用书写机不需要的软件类别。

我按照Veronica的博客文章安装了Debian，没有任何桌面环境和kmscon。 我对 Veronica 的第一个消遣是使用 emacs。 我只是快速地从 Git 中提取了我的主机上的 emacs 配置，并删除了所有有关编程的配置。 emacs 3 的启动速度极快，也应该如此。 您知道，人们在 80 年代末到 90 年代购买 386 是为了做类似的事情：启动 DOS 并使用 Word Perfect 或 Word Star 进行书写。 4 i5 机器不可能完美地做到这一点，因为它可能比 386 好 1000 倍。

通过我自己的配置，它还拥有我编写所需的所有 emacs 包。 事实上，没有那么多：我只需要灵巧地组织我的文件和 Markdown 模式（抱歉我不使用 org 模式）。 我在那里写作感觉很自在。 我不想浪费很多时间定制。 所以我什至不想安装 vterm 并简单地使用 eshell，因为我可能不需要做很多命令行工作。 机器现在直接启动到 emacs（只需将 emacs 放入 .bashrc 中）。 更具体地说，直接到 deft （只需将 (deft) 添加到我的 emacs 配置文件中）。

维罗妮卡的另一个转移是我如何将文本文件从书写机转移到其他机器。 我不想设置同步来跨机器同步文本文件。 我什至不想在我的任何计算机上安装 ssh 服务器。 我的过度解决方案是只拥有一个 Git 存储库并在 Codeberg 上拥有一个远程服务器。 Magit 在这里也很有用，可以进一步减少命令行的使用。 只是我对Git的使用缺乏想象力。 也许将来我会有类似 rsync 的东西。

然后，我写。 真是太棒了！ 它非常敏捷并且非常简单。 而且我可以真正专注于写作，而不是被 MS Teams 上关于我工作的废话分散注意力（和沮丧）。 我也不需要坐在我的“办公桌”周围。 我还可以一边看环法自行车赛，一边在沙发上写作。

我还想为此设置修复一些小问题。 一是kmscon 10.0.1的闪烁光标。 任何闪烁的光标都很容易让我感到沮丧。 我认为它会在下一个正式版本中修复。 我在官方 GitHub 存储库上看到了它。 5 另一个挑剔的是 emacs 主题。 许多 emacs 主题是为图形模式开发的。 我想使用明亮的主题（例如，日光照射）。 但在 kmscon 上显示效果很差。 但默认的深色主题就很好。

有了这个新的设置，我想我将能够完成积压的草稿以及一些新的学术写作任务。

  1. 我确实考虑过用 Raspberry Pi Zero 之类的东西为自己打造一台超大手持电脑的替代方案。 但经过自我反思，我不想制造更多的电子垃圾，因为我家里有足够的电子垃圾。 我应该重新利用一些原本属于电子废物的东西，这样它就不再是废物了。 ↩
  2. 我已经买了二手的。 ↩
  3. emacs 的速度相当快，我什至不用费心去设置 emacs 服务器。 而且我不需要经常启动 emacs。 ↩
  4. 一些著名作家仍然以这种方式写作。 最著名的当然是乔治·R. R。 Martin 和他装有 WordStar 的 DOS 计算机。 ↩
  5. 在书写机上编译kmscon对我来说太过分了。 所以，我就等待吧。 ↩
